title: I'll be going now
title_target: သွားတော့မယ်နော် — thwa:-dò.-mè-nò
goal: Wrapping up a conversation, writing a short message, and saying goodbye — then giving the farewell blessing people in Myanmar use to see off someone setting out on a long journey.
bekal: ending a conversation and saying goodbye naturally
writing a short message in Burmese
offering congratulations and good wishes with …ပါစေ

dialogs.title: စကားပြော — The last evening before going home
dialogs.intro: A year has gone by. Ani is going back to Indonesia, and Mya Mya and Ko Zaw are seeing her off. Watch for the closing phrases here — they're all set expressions, and all worth learning by heart.

lines.speaker: မြမြ:
lines.text: [မနက်ဖြန်|ma.nèk-hpyaⁿ] [ဘယ်နှစ်နာရီ|bè-hna.na-yee] [လေယာဉ်|lay-yiⁿ] [လဲ|lè:]။
lines.id: What time is your flight tomorrow?

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [မနက်|ma.nèk] [ခုနစ်နာရီခွဲ|hkoo.nik-na-yee-hkwè:] [ပါ|ba]။ [ငါးနာရီ|nga:-na-yee] [လောက်|lowk] [ထွက်|htwèk] [ရ|ya.] [မယ်|mè]။
lines.id: Seven thirty in the morning. I'll have to leave around five.
lines.literal: morning — seven-hour-half — polite. five-hour — about — go-out — must — will.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [ကျွန်တော်|cha.nò] [လေဆိပ်|lay-hsayk] [လိုက်|laik] [ပို့|poh.] [ပါ့မယ်|ba.-mè]။
lines.id: I'll take you to the airport.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [အားနာ|a:-na] [လိုက်တာ|laik-ta]။ [စောစော|sò-sò] [ကြီး|chee:] [ပါ|ba]။
lines.id: Oh, I feel bad. It's so early.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [ကိစ္စ|kayk-sa.] [မ|ma.] [ရှိ|shee.] [ပါဘူး|ba-boo:]။ [တစ်နှစ်|ta.hnik] [လုံး|lohⁿ:] [အတူတူ|a.too-doo] [အလုပ်|a.lohk] [လုပ်|lohk] [ခဲ့|hkè.] [တာ|da]။
lines.id: No problem. We've worked together for a whole year.
lines.literal: matter — not — be — polite-not. one-year — whole — together — work — do — back-then — thing.

lines.speaker: မြမြ:
lines.text: [အာနီ|a-nee] [ပြန်|pyaⁿ] [သွား|thwa:] [ရင်|yiⁿ] [လွမ်း|lwaⁿ:] [မယ်|mè]။
lines.id: We'll miss you when you've gone home, Ani.
lines.literal: ani — return — go — if — miss — will.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ကျွန်မ|cha.ma.] [လည်း|lè:] [လွမ်း|lwaⁿ:] [မယ်|mè]။ [တစ်နှစ်|ta.hnik] [လုံး|lohⁿ:] [ကျေးဇူး|chay:-zoo:] [အရမ်း|a.yaⁿ:] [တင်|tiⁿ] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။
lines.id: I'll miss you too. Thank you so much for this year.
lines.literal: I(f) — also — miss — will. one-year — whole — kindness — very — lean-on — polite-statement.

lines.speaker: မြမြ:
lines.text: [မြန်မာစကား|myaⁿ-ma-za.ga:] [တော်တော်|tò-dò] [တော်|tò] [သွား|thwa:] [ပြီ|bee] [နော်|nò]။
lines.id: Your Burmese has got a lot better, hasn't it?
lines.literal: myanmar-language — fairly — be-clever — go — already — right.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [မြမြ|mya.mya.] [တို့|doh.] [ကြောင့်|chowⁿ.] [ပါ|ba]။ [နောက်နှစ်|nowk-hnik] [ပြန်|pyaⁿ] [လာ|la] [ဖို့|hpoh.] [ကြိုးစား|choh:-sa:] [မယ်|mè]။
lines.id: Thanks to you all. I'll try to come back next year.
lines.literal: mya-mya — plural — because — polite. year-next — again — come — to — try — will.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [ဖုန်း|hpohⁿ:] [ဆက်|hsèk] [ပါ|ba] [နော်|nò]။ [စာ|sa] [လည်း|lè:] [ရေး|yay:] [ပါ|ba]။
lines.id: Call me, okay? And send messages too.
lines.literal: phone — connect — polite — okay. letter — also — write — polite.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ဟုတ်ကဲ့|hohk-kè.]။ [အမေ|a.may] [ကို|koh] [လည်း|lè:] [နှုတ်ဆက်|hnohk-hsèk] [ပေး|pay:] [ပါ|ba] [နော်|nò]။
lines.id: Okay. Give my regards to your mom.
lines.literal: true-yes. mother — to — also — greeting — give — polite — okay.

lines.speaker: မြမြ:
lines.text: [ဟုတ်ကဲ့|hohk-kè.]။ [ခရီး|hka.yee:] [ချောမွေ့|hchò-mway.] [ပါစေ|ba-zay]။ [ကျန်းမာ|chaⁿ:-ma] [ပါစေ|ba-zay] [နော်|nò]။
lines.id: Will do. Have a safe trip. Stay well, okay?
lines.literal: journey — smooth — may-it. healthy — may-it — okay.

grammars.title: Saying goodbye and closing a conversation
body: Burmese has no single word for "goodbye" that works in every situation. Instead, people say what is actually happening — the person leaving says "I'm off now", and the one staying answers.

head: Burmese
Say it
Who says it
rows: the one leaving — "I'll be going now"
ပြန်တော့မယ်
the one leaving — "I'm heading home now"
the one staying — "take care on the way"
နောက်မှ တွေ့မယ်

after: ⚠️ **တော့** (*dò.*) slotted in before မယ် means "now, at last" — it marks that the moment has come. သွားမယ် means "will go"; သွားတော့မယ် means "it's time for me to go". This little word is what makes your goodbye sound natural.

grammars.title: …ပါစေ — blessings and wishes
body: ပါစေ (*ba-zay*) closes a sentence and turns it into a blessing. This form has already appeared twice in the book, and now it's time to use it yourself.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: ကျန်းမာပါစေ
ကံကောင်းပါစေ
မြန်မြန် သက်သာပါစေ
အောင်မြင်ပါစေ

after: Farewell blessings are a sincere part of Burmese manners, not mere small talk. Saying ကျန်းမာပါစေ to someone about to travel far — especially with both hands slightly raised — will be received very warmly.

grammars.title: Sending regards and keeping in touch
body: A few set phrases for staying in touch after parting. Notice the pattern **…ကို … ပေးပါ**, meaning "please pass on … to …".

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: အမေကို နှုတ်ဆက်ပေးပါ
give my regards to your mom
ဖုန်း ဆက်ပါ
အဆက်အသွယ် မပြတ်ပါစေ

after: ⚠️ **လွမ်းတယ်** (*lwaⁿ:-dè*) is missing a person or place far away — a feeling people in Myanmar express very often, and not considered too personal to tell a friend or coworker.

grammars.title: …ဖို့ and …ကြောင့် — in order to, and thanks to
body: The last two markers in this book. **ဖို့** (*hpoh.*) expresses purpose, **ကြောင့်** (*chowⁿ.*) expresses a cause that is a person or thing.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: သင်ဖို့ အချိန် မရှိဘူး

after: Keep **ကြောင့်** apart from **လို့** (unit 18): ကြောင့် attaches to **a thing or person**, လို့ attaches to **a verb**. မိုးကြောင့် (because of the rain, as a thing) versus မိုးရွာလို့ (because it rained, as an action).

sections.title: A farewell conversation from start to finish

blocks.text: Here is a complete farewell, built entirely from sentences you've learned across the twenty units of this book. Read it aloud and notice how much of it already feels familiar.

head: Part
Burmese
Say it
rows: အားလုံးအတွက် ကျေးဇူးတင်ပါတယ်။
အရမ်း လွမ်းမယ်။
ဖုန်း ဆက်ပါ့မယ်။
မိသားစုကို နှုတ်ဆက်ပေးပါ။
ကျန်းမာပါစေ။

blocks.title: Congratulations for every occasion
items: **မွေးနေ့ မင်္ဂလာပါ** (*mway:-nay. miⁿ-ga-la-ba*) — happy birthday. Notice that the မင်္ဂလာပါ you learned in unit 1 turns up again here: the word really means "blessing", and it's used for every kind of congratulations.
**နှစ်သစ်ကူး မင်္ဂလာပါ** (*hnik-thik-koo: …*) — happy new year. Used both for the January New Year and for သင်္ကြန်.
**မင်္ဂလာဆောင် မင်္ဂလာပါ** — congratulations on your wedding.
**ဂုဏ်ယူပါတယ်** (*gohⁿ-yoo-ba-dè*) — congratulations, I'm proud of you. Used for graduations, promotions, and other successes. Notice ဂုဏ် — from the Pali *guṇa*, "virtue, merit".

blocks.text: Twenty units done. You began this book seeing Burmese script as rows of circles, and now you can read it, build full sentences with their endings, tell about a day gone by, order food, bargain at the market, decline politely, and give a farewell blessing. Only one thing is left: use it. **ကံကောင်းပါစေ** — good luck.
